PROJECTS

The majlis server (2024 - now)
An old office PC under my desk that serves my family and a few friends.
- Runs Debian and hosts the family photo library, my mother's recipe site and a network-wide ad blocker, each one in its own container and all of them started from a single compose file.
- Rebuilding the whole machine is one command: a set of playbooks installs the packages, creates the users and brings every service back. I proved it by wiping the disk twice.
- A small shell script checks every five minutes that each service answers, and sends me a Telegram message when one does not.
- Photos are copied every night to a second disk and once a week to my brother's house in Buraydah.

Publishing the club website without FTP (2026)
- Moved the Hail Tech Club website to the AWS free tier: the pages sit in a storage bucket behind the content delivery network.
- Every merge into the main branch now builds the site and publishes it by itself, so members no longer upload files by hand; a broken build is never published.
- Wrote a two-page guide so that the next committee can keep it running.
